newsitem.title: FRANCE: OECD votes to admit South Korea.
newsitem.headline: OECD votes to admit South Korea.

text.p: The Organisation for Economic Co-Operation and Development (OECD) voted on Friday morning to offer membership to South Korea, an OECD spokeswoman said.

A ceremony marking the formal invitation to South Korea to become a member of the OECD is scheduled for October 25, when South Korean foreign minister Gong Ro-Myung and OECD secretary general Donald Johnston will sign the agreement, she said.
The invitation makes South Korea the second Asian nation, after Japan, in the club of the world's economic establishment. Its admission will bring the number of member countries to 29.
Australia and New Zealand are also members from the Asia-Pacific region.

Korean membership will become effective after the government has ratified the OECD convention with the French government, which is depositary of the convention. During the period between the invitation and the ratification, the South Korean government will be able to participate in OECD's work as an observer.
